Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 26, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Shu'ara' (The Poets), because it is unique among the surahs of the Noble Qur'an in mentioning the misguided poets and the faithful poets, and describing their condition.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Discussion of the prophets and messengers whom Allah sent to guide humanity throughout the ages, and an account of some of what occurred between the prophets and their peoples. Along the way, it establishes Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah), the Resurrection, and the Reckoning, and clarifies the condition of the deniers and their final outcome.

• Praise of the Qur'an, a hint at the inability of the disbelievers to produce its like, mention of the proofs that it is from Allah, a response to the disbelievers' slanders against the Qur'an, and affirmation that it is free from being poetry or the words of the devils, and a warning to the polytheists that they will face the wrath of Allah, exalted is He.

• The command to the Messenger ﷺ to rely upon Allah in his call and in all his affairs, his charge to warn the people, and that his duty is only to convey (the message).

[Tafsir]

﴿Ta Sin Mim﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) has already been given at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.
These are the verses of the Qur'an, the clear one that explains everything, the criterion that distinguishes guidance from misguidance.

"Perhaps you, O Messenger, are destroying yourself out of your intense eagerness for their guidance, because they have not believed in you nor acted upon your guidance. So do not do that."
